summary: Attacked the Homological algebra area: EnhancedDerivedSheaves (11 stages), DGAInfinity (12), GrothendieckEulerForms (8), ProfiniteCohomology (14) and StablePeriodicCurved (9). No finding. The two within-area overlaps that looked like duplication are explicit imports, named in the roadmap text and recorded as links; all 54 stages carry library-coverage entries from two merged audits; every reference in the area resolves; and none of the 21 duplicate entries on the area's layers has both endpoints inside it, which is the right record for supplier relations.
checked: All five roadmaps and their 54 stages, with their documents.

The sharpest within-area duplication candidate: DGAInfinity Layer 10, 'K₀(Perf), Euler and numerical forms', against the whole of GrothendieckEulerForms, whose Layer 7 is 'left and right numerical Grothendieck groups'. It is an import, not a duplication, and the roadmap says so: Layer 10 tells the worker to 'compare this pairing and `K₀(Perf A)` with the Cartan/Ext-Euler constructions of the dependency roadmap' and to 'Form the left and right numerical quotients by the radicals from the dependency roadmap', and the DGAInfinity document names that roadmap, 'the [Grothendieck groups] roadmap supplies ordinary exact and triangulated `K₀`'.

The second: DGAInfinity's curved and Koszul material against StablePeriodicCurved Layers 5 and 6, curved DG algebras and derived categories of the second kind. Also coordination: the StablePeriodicCurved link map records DGAInfinity Layer 0 and Layer 1 as suppliers of its Layer 5, and DGAInfinity Layer 5 as a supplier of its Layer 4.

Whether those dependencies are recorded machine-readably rather than only in prose, which is where a sister area failed. They are: twelve links have both endpoints inside this area, including four into DGAInfinity Layer 10 from GrothendieckEulerForms Layers 2, 4, 5 and 7, one into DGAInfinity Layer 11 from its Layer 3, and one into DGAInfinity Layer 7 from its Layer 2. Link maps exist for GrothendieckEulerForms, ProfiniteCohomology and StablePeriodicCurved.

Whether the two roadmaps without a link map are therefore unrecorded, which is the shape of a real finding elsewhere. Neither is. DGAInfinity's relations are carried by the GrothendieckEulerForms and StablePeriodicCurved packets. EnhancedDerivedSheaves is a campaign roadmap and uses the campaign mechanism instead: all 11 of its stages populate `requires`, it carries 93 stage edges, and its 28 consumers are recorded on both sides, 28 roadmaps naming it as a prerequisite and its own consumers field listing 28.
Reference resolution across the area: every roadmap-level prerequisite and every stage `requires` entry resolves, with two UPSTREAM sentinels in EnhancedDerivedSheaves E0, which is house practice.

Library coverage: all 54 stages of all five roadmaps carry an entry in data/library-coverage.json, from AUDIT-22 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves, DGAInfinity, GrothendieckEulerForms) and AUDIT-23 (ProfiniteCohomology, StablePeriodicCurved). Neither audit is in the pendingReview list, so both are merged.

The duplicate records themselves: the area's layers carry 21 duplicate entries, and not one has both endpoints inside the area. That is the correct record, since the within-area relations are supplier and consumer rather than layers stating the same target, and they are carried as links instead.

Disclosure rather than a check: I red-teamed AUDIT-23 earlier in this session (RT-AUDIT-23), which audits ProfiniteCohomology and StablePeriodicCurved among its five roadmaps. That is a different deliverable and I wrote neither the audit nor these roadmaps, so it is not a conflict the rules name, but a reader should know that my familiarity with two of these five roadmaps comes from that job, and that the finding I raised there concerned a stage of a different roadmap in the same audit.
